# Period evidence register

<!-- Generated from kit/evidence/register.json by kit/evidence/build-register-doc.mjs. Edit the data, then run the script; do not edit this file by hand. -->

This register has one row for each rule about how Windows 95 looked or behaved that GUI95 has a source for: 200 rules, compiled on 2026-11-19 against kit 1.1.2. Each row says what the rule is, where it comes from, how sure we are, and whether the GUI95 kit follows it.

**What it is not.** It records what written sources and reimplementations say, and what the kit does. It is not a certification of fidelity. Nothing in it has yet been compared with a real Windows 95 system: the sources are two Microsoft books, one book by a Windows 95 designer, Microsoft's File Manager templates, and the Wine and ReactOS reimplementations, which are not Microsoft code and also follow later Windows versions. A capture of a real system is planned and is expected to confirm some rows and correct others.

The books are in copyright and the source code is under the LGPL and GPL, so the register states facts and cites locations; it does not reproduce passages or code.

Agents can query the same data with the `get_gui95_period_rules` tool of the [MCP service](mcp-service.md), and code can use [`kit/evidence/register.mjs`](../kit/evidence/register.mjs); see [build-kit evidence](build-kit-evidence.md#the-period-evidence-register). For the sources themselves, see the [reading shelf](historical-sources.md) and the [bibliography](bibliography.md).

## How to read a row

- **Era** says which system the rule belongs to. A row marked *Draft only* is a statement from the February 1995 draft that the final book changed; a *Windows 3.x* row is there so the fact is not mistaken for Windows 95.
- **Confidence** is high, medium or low, with a reason. Agreement between independent sources raises it. Where sources contradict each other the row says so and stays low; nothing was resolved by guessing.
- **Evidence** is one of: stated in the text; read from a figure; structural, from source code; inferred; measured.
- **Sources** give a location precise enough to check: a section file and title of the final guidelines (with the printed page where known), a PDF page, or a file, function and line. "(checked)" means that while compiling the register at least one of the cited locations in that entry was read against the source and said what the rule states. Line numbers refer to the Wine and ReactOS master branches as retrieved on 18 November 2026, so the linked files may have moved on.
- **Kit** is the status of the kit against the rule, the stylesheet rule or function looked at, and whether it was rendered and measured in Chromium at device scale 1 or read from the code. *Not applicable* means the rule is for an application's own design or wording, or for a control the browser draws; *not implemented* means the kit could follow it but has nothing for it yet.
- No row has been verified by the review that commissioned the research notes; that field is false throughout and is kept for later use.

## Unintended differences that remain

Ordered by how visible each is, then by confidence. This is the to-do list. Each is a place where the kit could follow the rule and does not, with no record that the difference was chosen.

| Rule | Control | Visibility | Confidence | What the kit does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [A pop-up menu item is the text height plus a few pixels: 17 px](#menu-item-height) | menu | obvious | high | Items render 22 px high: five pixels taller per item. |
| [List box rows are exactly the font height, with text 1 px from the left](#list-box-row-height) | list-box | visible | high | Rows measure 16.84 px (11 px text at line-height 1.35 plus 1 px padding above and below) and text starts 3 px in. The fractional height can blur the edges of the selection bar. |
| [Related toolbar buttons touch; groups are separated](#toolbar-button-spacing) | toolbar | visible | high | gap: 2 px separates every button, related or not; there is no group separator. |
| [A group box caption starts 7 px in and clears 1 px of frame each side](#group-box-caption-position) | group-box | visible | high | Caption text starts 13 px from the frame's left (8 px fieldset padding, 4 px legend padding), four pixels further right than the capture, with 4 px cleared each side. That position is kept until the density decision. The caption interrupts both lines of the frame, as in the capture. |
| [The default slider thumb is pointed toward its tick marks](#slider-thumb-pointed) | slider | visible | medium | The thumb is always a rectangle, which is the both-sides variant only. |
| [Text in a text box starts 3 px from the control's edge](#text-box-text-inset) | text-box | subtle | high | padding 4 px 5 px: text starts 5 px in, two further than the rule. |
| [A closed drop-down list is 21 px high whatever height it is given](#drop-down-list-height) | drop-down-list | subtle | high | The kit's drop-down list renders 23 px high, the same as its text boxes: two pixels taller than the capture. |
| [Unavailable arrows are engraved in white and shadow](#arrows-unavailable-engraved) | spin-box | subtle | high | Up-down and drop-down arrows are fixed after 1.1.2: shadow where the black arrow was, with a white copy one pixel down and right (the lowest row of the copy is hidden by the edge of a 10 px up-down button). Scroll bar arrows remain: the kit has no unavailable artwork for them, and headless Chromium does not draw scroll bars, so no state of theirs could be rendered here. |
| [The menu bar is 19 px high with 18 px items](#menu-bar-height) | menu-bar | subtle | high | The bar renders 22 px with 20 px titles: three and two pixels taller. |
| [The title bar is 18 or 19 px high; the references disagree](#title-bar-height) | title-bar | subtle | high | The kit's title bar renders 20 px high: two pixels taller than the 18 px bar. |
| [Caption buttons sit 2 px from the top and right of the title bar](#caption-button-inset) | title-bar | subtle | high | Buttons render 3 px from the top and 3 px from the right of a 20 px bar, one pixel more each way than the capture. |
| [Toolbar buttons are 24 × 22 (and 32 × 30) pixels](#toolbar-button-size) | toolbar | subtle | high | A toolbar button renders 24 × 23: the general 23 px button minimum makes it one pixel taller than the rule. |
| [The focus rectangle appears on mouse press as well as keyboard navigation](#focus-shown-on-mouse-press) | all | subtle | high | The focus rectangle is tied to :focus-visible, which browsers do not apply to buttons, check boxes or option buttons focused with the mouse. |
| [A progress bar never shows a partial block mid-bar](#progress-bar-whole-blocks) | progress | subtle | medium | The repeating gradient is clipped at the exact value: at 45% of an 84 px bar the last block is 6 px wide. |
| [A dialog's margin is 7 dialog units](#dialog-margin) | dialog | subtle | medium | padding 8 px, which is about 5 dialog units: narrower than either source. |
| [Arrow keys on a tab stop at the first and last tab](#tab-arrows-stop-at-ends) | tabs | subtle | medium | Fixed after 1.2.0 for Left and Right, which now stop at the ends, with Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Page Up and Down still going round. Up and Down still move between tabs, which the real control does not do. |
| [A latched toolbar button has the field's sunken order, not the push button's](#edge-toolbar-latched) | toolbar | subtle | low | Since 1.1.2 every held or latched button, toolbar buttons included, takes --gui95-pressed: black outside, shadow inside. Before 1.1.2 the kit drew shadow outside, black inside, which is what this source describes for toolbars. The checkerboard matches. |
| [The focus rectangle sits directly inside a push button's bevel](#button-focus-rectangle-inset) | push-button | invisible | high | outline-offset −4 px puts the dots on the fourth pixel, which matches an ordinary button. On a default button the dots should be on the fifth pixel; the kit keeps them on the fourth, directly against the bevel. |
| [The gap between a check box and its label is half a digit's width](#check-box-label-gap) | check-box | invisible | high | margin-right 4 px: one pixel narrower than the 5 px the capture shows. |
| [Menu text starts after a check-mark column: about 20 px from the menu edge](#menu-text-inset) | menu | invisible | high | Text starts 26 px from the menu edge (3 px menu padding plus 23 px item padding) and the check mark 10 px: one pixel further right than the capture. Read from the atlas rendering; the atlas has no label text. |
| [A menu separator is a 9 px item with an etched line inset 1 px each side](#menu-separator) | menu | invisible | high | Renders 8 px in all (3 px margin, 2 px line, 3 px margin), one pixel shorter, and the line is inset one pixel from the item's left edge where Windows has none. The line's offset from the top, three pixels, matches. |
| [The up arrow sits one row higher than the down arrow, and both one column left of centre](#scroll-arrow-glyph-position) | scroll-bar | invisible | high | Centred artwork lands on rows 6–9 and columns 5–11 for both arrows: the rows match the capture and both arrows are one pixel right. |
| [Status bar panes start at the left edge, 2 px below the top](#status-bar-left-inset) | status-bar | invisible | medium | The first pane renders 2 px in from the left edge where the capture has none, and the bar has 2 px below the panes where the capture has none (22 px high against 20). The 2 px top border and the 2 px gap match. |

| [The ellipsis is three periods closed up against the label](#wording-ellipsis-form) | medium |

## Focus and keyboard

| Rule | Era and confidence | Sources | Kit |

| <a id="button-focus-rectangle-inset"></a>**The focus rectangle sits directly inside a push button's bevel**<br>`button-focus-rectangle-inset` · push-button<br>Keyboard focus on a push button is a dotted rectangle on the fourth pixel in from the button's edge, leaving one face pixel between the bevel and the dots. On a default button it is on the fifth pixel, again one pixel inside the bevel.<br>*Note.* Wine and ReactOS put the rectangle one pixel further out than the capture shows. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: measured | Wine: [dlls/user32/button.c, lines 798–801 (PB_Paint())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/user32/button.c)<br>Final guidelines: [S118DC.htm, "Visual States for Controls"](https://techshelps.github.io/MSDN/WINGUIDE/S118DC.htm)<br>February draft: [PDF p. 296](https://ics.uci.edu/~kobsa/courses/ICS104/course-notes/Microsoft_WindowsGuidelines.pdf#page=296)<br>Windows 95 capture: 24-bit capture, sheet 2 button_focus (dots on row and column 3) and button_default_focus (row and column 4) (checked) | **differs (unintended)** (invisible)<br>outline-offset −4 px puts the dots on the fourth pixel, which matches an ordinary button. On a default button the dots should be on the fifth pixel; the kit keeps them on the fourth, directly against the bevel.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · :focus-visible` (rendered, 2026-11-19) |
| <a id="check-option-focus-on-label"></a>**Focus on a check box or option button is drawn round its label**<br>`check-option-focus-on-label` · check-box<br>When a check box or option button has the keyboard focus, the dotted rectangle surrounds the label text, one pixel wider than the text on each side, not the box or circle. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: structural, from source code | Wine: [dlls/user32/button.c, lines 934–939 (CB_Paint())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/user32/button.c) (checked)<br>Windows 95 capture: 24-bit capture, sheet 2 check_focus and radio_checked_focus (checked) | **matches**<br>Fixed after 1.1.2. A label that wraps its box as first child, or follows it as the next element, carries a dotted rectangle from one pixel left of the text to one pixel right of it, and the box has none. A box with no label keeps a rectangle round the box. A label stretched by a layout container narrows to its text while focused. Shown for :focus-visible only (see focus-shown-on-mouse-press). The rectangle is the height of the label's box, which for a label wrapping onto several inline lines is not the text block.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · label:has(>input:first-child:focus-visible)::after`, `kit/components/gui95.css · input:focus-visible+label::after` (rendered, 2026-11-18) |
| <a id="drop-down-focus-highlight"></a>**A focused drop-down list shows its value in the selection colours**<br>`drop-down-focus-highlight` · drop-down-list<br>When a closed drop-down list has the focus, its text area is filled with the highlight colour, the text is drawn in the highlighted-text colour, and the focus rectangle surrounds the text area only, not the button. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: structural, from source code | Wine: [dlls/user32/combo.c, lines 718–738 (CBPaintText())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/user32/combo.c) (checked)<br>Windows 95 capture: 24-bit capture, sheet 2 combo_droplist_focus: one window-colour pixel inside the edge, then the highlight with an inverted dotted rectangle on its outline; the button untouched (checked) | **matches**<br>Fixed after 1.1.2. With the focus and the list closed, the text area (3 px in from the control's edge, ending one pixel short of the button) is navy with white text and a dotted rectangle on its outline; the button is untouched and the control has no outer outline. Where the engine supports :open the highlight is dropped while the list is open. The dots are white on navy, the kit's convention for a rectangle on a selected row; Windows drew the rectangle by inverting pixels.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · select:not([multiple]):not([size]):is(:focus-visible,[data-gui95-state="focused"])` (rendered, 2026-11-18) |
| <a id="drop-down-list-height"></a>**A closed drop-down list is 21 px high whatever height it is given**<br>`drop-down-list-height` · drop-down-list<br>A closed drop-down list sets its own height from its font: the text height plus 8, which is 21 px with 8-point MS Sans Serif, not the 23 px of a text box or button beside it. Its button is 16 px wide and 17 high inside the 2 px sunken edge.<br>*Note.* The final guidelines give drop-down lists the same 14 dialog units as buttons; the real control ignores the height it is given. See button-height-14-dlu. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: measured | Windows 95 capture: Report [sheet2] combo_droplist=8,160,84,21, fieldheight=15, itemheight=13; 24-bit capture, sheet 2 combo_* (checked) | **differs (unintended)** (subtle)<br>The kit's drop-down list renders 23 px high, the same as its text boxes: two pixels taller than the capture.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · select`, `kit/test/baseline/state-atlas.png · select-drop-down-list` (rendered, 2026-11-19) |

| <a id="list-box-row-height"></a>**List box rows are exactly the font height, with text 1 px from the left**<br>`list-box-row-height` · list-box<br>A list box row is as high as the font's text height (13 px for 8-point MS Sans Serif) with no extra padding, and item text starts one pixel from the row's left edge.<br>*Note.* The fractional line box comes from the kit's 11px/1.35 font setting and affects every text row, not only list boxes. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: structural, from source code | Wine: [dlls/user32/listbox.c, lines 1409–1415 (LISTBOX_SetFont())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/user32/listbox.c) (checked)<br>Wine: [dlls/user32/listbox.c, lines 700–709 (LISTBOX_PaintItem())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/user32/listbox.c)<br>Windows 95 capture: Report [sheet2] list_select.itemheight=13; 24-bit capture, sheet 2 list_select (rows of 13, first ink 2 px from the row's left) (checked) | **differs (unintended)** (visible)<br>Rows measure 16.84 px (11 px text at line-height 1.35 plus 1 px padding above and below) and text starts 3 px in. The fractional height can blur the edges of the selection bar.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · [role="option"]` (rendered, 2026-11-18) |

| <a id="list-left-margin"></a>**Text in a list or inset box needs about half an "n" of left margin**<br>`list-left-margin` · list-box<br>A too-narrow left margin in lists is one of the commonest faults in Windows interfaces; leave roughly half the width of a lowercase "n" between an inset box's edge and its text.<br>*Note.* This recommendation and list-box-row-height pull in different directions: the stock control is tighter than Howlett advises. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**medium**: A designer's recommendation, not a system metric; Wine's own list box uses a 1 px inset.<br>Evidence: stated in the text | Howlett: fig. 6.15 caption; PDF p. 90 (printed p. 78) | **matches**<br>Text starts 5 px from the control's edge: 2 px edge and 3 px padding.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · [role="listbox"]`, `kit/components/gui95.css · [role="option"]` (rendered, 2026-11-18) |

| <a id="drop-down-list-keys"></a>**A closed drop-down list changes value with the arrow keys; Esc on the open list does not restore**<br>`drop-down-list-keys` · drop-down-list<br>With the list closed, Up, Down, Home, End, Page Up and letters change the value at once. | <a id="menu-item-height"></a>**A pop-up menu item is the text height plus a few pixels: 17 px**<br>`menu-item-height` · menu<br>A menu item is as high as the larger of the text height plus 2 and the character height plus 4, which is 17 px with the default menu font. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: structural, from source code | Wine: [dlls/win32u/menu.c, line 2163 (calc_menu_item_size())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/win32u/menu.c) (checked)<br>ReactOS: [win32ss/user/ntuser/menu.c, lines 1978–1979 (MENU_CalcItemSize())](https://github.com/reactos/reactos/blob/master/win32ss/user/ntuser/menu.c)<br>Windows 95 capture: Report [sheet3] menu.item0 to menu.item8 (17 px each); 24-bit capture, sheet 3 menu, highlighted item 17 rows (checked) | **differs (unintended)** (obvious)<br>Items render 22 px high: five pixels taller per item.<br>Looked at: `kit/components/gui95.css · [role^="menuitem"]`, `kit/test/baseline/state-atlas.png · menu.menuitem0` (rendered, 2026-11-19) |
| <a id="menu-text-inset"></a>**Menu text starts after a check-mark column: about 20 px from the menu edge**<br>`menu-text-inset` · menu<br>On Windows 95 OSR2.5 the first ink of an item's label is 25 px from the pop-up menu's outer edge (22 px from the item's edge; items sit inside a 3 px margin), and the 7 px check mark starts 9 px from the menu's edge. Wine's formula gives about 20 px. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Measured on Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5), whose user and gdi files are version 4.0.0.950 like the 1995 release; not measured on the 1995 original.<br>Evidence: measured | Wine: [dlls/win32u/menu.c, lines 2663–2665 (draw_menu_item()); lines 3067–3069 (calc_popup_menu_size())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/win32u/menu.c)<br>Wine: [dlls/win32u/menu.c, line 128](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/win32u/menu.c) (checked)<br>ReactOS: [win32ss/user/ntuser/menu.c, lines 2480–2482 (MENU_DrawMenuItem())](https://github.com/reactos/reactos/blob/master/win32ss/user/ntuser/menu.c)<br>Wine: [dlls/win32u/sysparams.c, lines 7228–7238 (get_system_metrics())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/win32u/sysparams.c)<br>Windows 95 capture: 24-bit capture, sheet 3 menu: first ink of "New" at column 25 of the menu, check mark at columns 9 to 15 (checked) | **differs (unintended)** (invisible)<br>Text starts 26 px from the menu edge (3 px menu padding plus 23 px item padding) and the check mark 10 px: one pixel further right than the capture. | <a id="menu-shortcut-column"></a>**Shortcut keys are left-aligned in one shared column**<br>`menu-shortcut-column` · menu<br>The text after the tab in a menu item, normally its shortcut key, is drawn left-aligned at a column position shared by every item in the menu. Right alignment happens only with a different separator character. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Two independent reimplementations agree on the structure; neither is Microsoft code and both follow later Windows versions too.<br>Evidence: structural, from source code | Wine: [dlls/win32u/menu.c, lines 2723–2731 (draw_menu_item())](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/dlls/win32u/menu.c) (checked)<br>ReactOS: [win32ss/user/ntuser/menu.c, lines 2050–2053 (MENU_PopupMenuCalcSize())](https://github.com/reactos/reactos/blob/master/win32ss/user/ntuser/menu.c) | **matches**<br>Fixed after 1.1.2. When a menu opens the component measures its shortcuts and gives every shortcut box the width of the widest, so "Ctrl+O" and "Ctrl+Shift+S" start at the same x and the longest ends at the right edge. | <a id="menu-cascade-time-out"></a>**A cascading menu opens, and closes, after a short time-out**<br>`menu-cascade-time-out` · menu<br>A cascading (sub) menu appears a short time after the pointer rests on its parent item, and is removed a short time after the pointer moves to another item, so the user can drag diagonally into it.<br>*Note.* Found while compiling the register; the research notes listed the rule as unchanged between editions but did not compare the kit. Windows 95 has no setting to read for this delay (SPI_GETMENUSHOWDELAY is refused), so it was measured: 400 ms, or 400 ms plus a timer tick or two when the pointer was still settling. | Windows 95 (1995)<br>**high**: Stated in both editions of the guidelines.<br>Evidence: stated in the text | Final guidelines: [S11860.htm, "Cascading Menus"](https://techshelps.github.io/MSDN/WINGUIDE/S11860.htm) (checked)<br>February draft: [PDF p. 114](https://ics.uci.edu/~kobsa/courses/ICS104/course-notes/Microsoft_WindowsGuidelines.pdf#page=114)<br>Windows 95 recording: tools/win95-reference/recordings/menu-mouse.json: steps 3 and 10: a cascading menu was told to open 400, 491 and 493 ms after the pointer first highlighted its parent item, on the guest's clock (checked) | **matches**<br>Fixed after 1.1.2. The highlight follows the pointer at once; a submenu opens after the pointer has rested 400 ms on its parent item, and an open one closes 400 ms after the pointer moves to a sibling unless the pointer reaches the submenu first.
